transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-12 14:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Solarwave CTO), Liam O'Connor (Head of Infra), Priya Raman (Security)

Summary: quick discovery focused on Private / VPC deployment options for Solarwave's inference workloads. Main topics: region constraints (EU), VPC peering vs PrivateLink/private endpoints, CIDR overlap concerns, egress/firewall rules, KMS and audit log requirements, timeline for pilot and benchmarking.

Topics: private endpoints, VPC peering, cross-account peering, region & data residency, SOC2/KMS, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, network egress, NAT and firewall considerations.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, account exec at Redwood Inference. With me is Sofia, our systems engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:06] Maya Chen: Hi Jordan, thanks. Doing well, morning for us. Happy to be here.
[00:09] Sofia Patel: Hi Maya, hi Liam, hi Priya, thanks for the time. We'll try to keep to 45-ish minutes and leave time for questions.
[00:16] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. We're mostly focused on private deployment options, networking, and region stuff.
[00:21] Jordan Lee: Perfect, that's what we wanted to dig into. Quick intro: Solarwave is evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — from what you shared in the form, you're leaning Private (VPC) because of data residency and compliance, correct?
[00:32] Maya Chen: Yes that's right. We have PHI-ish telemetry and customer identifiers, and legal wants all inference traffic to stay in EU. Also SOC2 is in progress and we have an internal KMS.
[00:43] Priya Raman: And we need audit logs, key separation, and no public egress to the internet for requests/response.
[00:50] Sofia Patel: Understood. Our Private option supports a VPC-connected deployment where the Redwood control plane is separated and the inference nodes run in your VPC or in a customer-dedicated environment, depending on the model. We commonly do two patterns: cross-account VPC peering (or AWS Resource Access Manager) and AWS PrivateLink / Interface Endpoints.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Can you explain pros/cons? We prefer minimal management overhead but security is top priority.
[01:10] Sofia Patel: Sure. VPC peering is simpler from a networking perspective if you control both accounts — low latency, direct routing — but requires non-overlapping CIDRs. PrivateLink gives you interface endpoints, more restrictive, and you don't need route table changes in the same way. PrivateLink is often preferred when teams want explicit endpoint-level control and to reduce blast radius.
[01:26] Liam O'Connor: Our infra uses 10.0.0.0/16 heavily across AWS org and we do have overlapping CIDRs in some environments, so peering might be tricky. Also we prefer eu-central-1 for compute locality.
[01:39] Sofia Patel: CIDR overlap is a common blocker for peering. Workarounds are either adjusting CIDRs, using transit gateway with NAT, or using PrivateLink which avoids direct route overlap. PrivateLink can be slightly more operationally heavy on our side to set up but gives clean isolation.
[01:55] Jordan Lee: Also, worth noting that for very latency-sensitive workloads we recommend a dedicated capacity deployment in the same region as the VPC — that reduces inter-region hops. But for strict compliance you can run inference inside a private VPC in your account.
[02:07] Maya Chen: If we run inside our VPC, can we bring our own KMS keys? We need to ensure Redwood cannot decrypt logs or payloads.
[02:15] Sofia Patel: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM in Private deployments. You can bring your own KMS keys; we support CMEK for model payloads and we can configure the nodes so encryption at rest uses your keys. We also can route audit logs to your CloudWatch or an S3 bucket with bucket policies that restrict access.
[02:31] Priya Raman: What about network egress — e.g., outbound requests from the inference nodes to get model binaries or updates — those need to be restricted.
[02:38] Sofia Patel: Good call. For Private we can pre-stage model artifacts in your S3 (signed URLs) and the inference nodes fetch them via VPC endpoints (S3 Gateway endpoints). For software updates we can use an allowlist and also have an option to air-gap updates for on-prem or very restricted customers. There's also a patch window we can coordinate.
[02:55] Liam O'Connor: Region availability: do you have images/AMIs in eu-central-1? We need to stay in that region for data residency.
[03:02] Jordan Lee: We do support eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for Private today, but capacity availability can vary. For Dedicated reserved capacity we can guarantee region placement via contract. For private self-managed deployments you control region and we provide the deployment artifacts. I'll flag capacity and confirm with infra team after the call.
[03:20] Maya Chen: Great. A few compliance Qs: SOC2, ISO, pen test reports — can we get those as part of the security pack?
[03:27] Jordan Lee: Absolutely, we'll send the security pack. It includes SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and our data handling and retention policies. For Private deployments we also provide architecture diagrams and a runbook.
[03:36] Priya Raman: How do you handle identity and RBAC? We use SAML/SSO and need SCIM provisioning ideally.
[03:43] Sofia Patel: We support SAML SSO, SCIM, and fine-grained RBAC. For Private we can integrate with your IdP and sync groups; we also support short-lived credentials for node access and optional bastion setups.
[03:53] Liam O'Connor: Latency numbers — can you share ballpark p99 tokens latency? We run real-time chat assistants so p99 matters.
[04:01] Sofia Patel: Ballpark depends on model and batch size. For typical Llama-family models on a 16G GPU instance we see token latencies in the tens to low hundreds of ms at small batch sizes. With dedicated capacity in-region you get the lowest variability. We'll capture a baseline in the SE deep-dive / benchmark call.
[04:19] Maya Chen: Pricing — we're trying to compare dedicated monthly committed vs private self-managed. Any notes on cost drivers?
[04:25] Jordan Lee: Main drivers are committed throughput (dedicated) vs actual usage (hosted), plus network egress and storage. Private self-managed has an infra cost on your side (EC2, EBS, NATs) plus a software/license fee. Dedicated gives predictable invoicing and we offload infra. We'll follow up with a cost model spreadsheet.
[04:41] Priya Raman: Logging: can we route audit logs to our SIEM?
[04:44] Sofia Patel: Yes, we can forward logs to your SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch or deliver S3 exports. You can manage retention and encryption with your S3 bucket and KMS.
[04:53] Jordan Lee: Quick recap of key blockers we heard: 1) CIDR overlap could prevent peering, 2) must run in eu-central-1, 3) need customer-managed KMS and audit log integration, 4) minimal public egress.
[05:06] Liam O'Connor: Correct. Also want to see a sample VPC peering diagram and PrivateLink setup and a runbook of the deployment steps.
[05:13] Sofia Patel: We'll send a VPC diagram and an example terraform snippet for the peering and endpoint configurations. We'll also include the checklist for IAM roles and security group rules.
[05:22] Maya Chen: Excellent. On timeline — we want a pilot in the next 4 weeks if the runbook looks good.
[05:27] Jordan Lee: That aligns. Action items and follow-ups we'll capture in the notes.
[05:31] Priya Raman: One more question — does Redwood keep model weights in your control? We are using open models but want to ensure no external copies are hosted outside the customer's environment in Private mode.
[05:40] Sofia Patel: In Private deployments where the runtime runs in your account, model weights are stored in customer-controlled S3 and only downloaded to nodes in your VPC. We can sign an appendix if you need explicit guarantees.
[05:50] Maya Chen: That sounds good.
[05:52] Jordan Lee: Great — we'll wrap up. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security pack, runbook, and pricing. Let's pencil the SE benchmark week of 5/25 pending CIDR info.
[05:59] Maya Chen: Thanks Jordan and Sofia.
[06:01] Liam O'Connor: Thanks, looking forward to the materials.

End of transcript.
